rationale: Residual-frontier feedback after the run's five confirmed findings. This turn read the remaining supporting paths that had not been examined - the shared utility helpers, the observer fan-out, the peers.json readers, the discard snapshot store, the FileSnapshotStore Open integrity check, the NewRaft startup ordering and the FSM apply paths - and no additional contract discrepancy was established in them. One reporting ambiguity is recorded as a specific unknown rather than as a Candidate, with the source that shows it, so it is not lost if the run ends.

feedback.answered: The supporting paths read this turn hold no further contract discrepancy: randomTimeout and the backoff helpers match their documented bounds, blocking observers are an explicit opt-in documented as able to block Raft, the peers.json readers validate the ingested configuration, the discard store returns the documented errors, FileSnapshotStore.Open verifies the stored CRC64 before returning the reader, NewRaft reads the last log before restoring the snapshot and its configuration scan starts above the snapshot index, and the FSM apply paths advance their index consistently for commands and stored configurations. One ambiguity remains in Raft.Restore: after the restore completes it applies a no-op and returns that future's error, so a leadership loss or enqueue timeout that prevents the no-op from committing is reported the same way as a failed restore, even though the FSM state was already replaced and the burned index advanced. The docs say only that the call blocks 'until the restore is complete or an error occurs', which does not distinguish the two, and the error is also the way the caller learns that the new state has not propagated to followers, so this is recorded as an unresolved reporting question rather than a defect.
remaining: Whether Raft.Restore should distinguish a completed restore whose confirmation no-op did not commit from a restore that failed before replacing the FSM, and whether callers rely on the current single error to decide re-issuing.

Unread or partially read areas outside the core: net_transport.go and tcp_transport.go RPC encoding and version negotiation, the FSM batch manager, NewRaft startup reconstruction, and the in-repository testing helpers.

The constructed-environment limits recorded on the five confirmed checks: whether production stores or leaders reach the same failure positions, and whether any of the confirmed defects also has a safety consequence rather than the bounded availability or contract consequence confirmed.
feedback.rationale: Recorded so the residual frontier is explicit: the core lines and every mapped surface have now been read, five responsibilities are confirmed in scope with executed witnesses, and what remains is a set of unread peripheral areas plus one reporting ambiguity that the source shows but does not settle. No map change is proposed because nothing in the accepted map is contradicted by this reading; the F-term-vote and core overview texts already state the persisted-term and recovery paths accurately.
